comments.note:
Full OWASP Top 10 review performed on the changed code. No security findings — all 10 categories reviewed; no Critical, High, or Medium issues identified. Detailed assessment below:

A01 (Broken Access Control): computeEffectiveStatus() is module-private (not exported), takes only boolean inputs derived from trusted local sources (OS process table + filesystem). No user-controlled input reaches the helper. Existing path-traversal guard in checkPathPrefix() (line 570) was unchanged.

A02 (Cryptographic Failures): No cryptographic operations involved. No secrets in scope.

A03 (Injection): computeEffectiveStatus() accepts two boolean parameters only — no string input, no injection vector.

A04 (Insecure Design): Refactor reduces duplication of security-relevant status logic, lowering the risk of logic drift across call sites. Net improvement.

A05 (Security Misconfiguration): No configuration changes.

A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components): No new dependencies introduced.

A07 (Identification & Authentication Failures): No authentication or session logic touched.

A08 (Software & Data Integrity Failures): No serialization/deserialization changes. Atomic write pattern (writeQueueFileAtomic) unchanged.

A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures): No logging changes.

A10 (SSRF): No network operations in the new or modified code paths.
